scope: Complete native Keeper, not an optional substitute for automatic recovery
design_to_validate: Keep existing daemon start receipts/identity; attach one background Keeper after native startup acceptance. Split internal start_daemon from public start so supervisor restart does not spawn supervisors recursively.

Give each Keeper an exclusive lifetime lock and generation-fenced process identity journal; bootstrap initial configuration over private stdin, then consume the committed protected restart config after owner death.
Persist user shutdown intent before acknowledgement and support stop while daemon is absent/backing off; a stopped service must not be resurrected.
Revalidate all ways configuration changes before relying on the checkpoint. Resume only last committed configuration; reconcile old execution proofs without replaying tasks.
Monitor process lifetime rather than treating observation timeout as death; use bounded crash backoff and explicit failed/suppressed states. Retain source/config errors for manual repair.

Test singleton startup, timeout without duplicate start, crash/queued work/callback continuity, stop race/backoff stop, reload-then-crash and Keeper loss. Validate real Herdr host/display boundaries separately.
